codeReview.summary: The ProxyFailureModal component is well-implemented with clean separation of concerns, proper event handling, and comprehensive test coverage. The component fulfills all VAL-FLR-002 requirements: modal appears on all-proxies-failed event, shows failed proxy list with status badges and cooldown ETAs, provides three action buttons (Continue without proxy, Retry with cooldown, Stop validation), and is non-dismissible except by choosing an option. The Dialog component was properly extended with a hideCloseButton prop. Integration with useEmailValidation hook via Tauri event listener is clean. The subsequent features (continue-without-proxy-option, retry-with-cooldown-option, stop-validation-option) further refined the handlers but the core modal UI from this feature remains intact and solid.

issues.description: The 'cannot be dismissed by clicking outside' test only asserts that the dialog is in the document — it doesn't actually verify that clicking outside is prevented. A more robust test would fire a pointerDown event on the overlay and verify the dialog remains open.
issues.suggestedFix: Consider adding a test that simulates a click outside the dialog and asserts the modal is still visible: fireEvent.pointerDown(document.body); expect(screen.getByText('All Proxies Unavailable')).toBeInTheDocument();

issues.description: The retryWithCooldown handler in the original commit used a blocking setTimeout (await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(...))) which would freeze the UI thread during the wait. This was later refactored in the retry-with-cooldown-option feature to use an interval-based countdown with status feedback. The original implementation was functional but not ideal UX.
issues.suggestedFix: Already addressed by the retry-with-cooldown-option feature which refactored to use setInterval with live countdown state.

issues.description: The continueWithoutProxy handler in the original commit called invoke('update_proxy_pool_config', { enabled: false }) which would permanently modify the user's proxy settings. This was later fixed in the continue-without-proxy-option feature to use a session-level bypass instead. The original implementation risked confusing users by permanently disabling their proxy setting.
issues.suggestedFix: Already addressed by the continue-without-proxy-option feature which uses a session-level bypass command.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The worker introduced a hideCloseButton prop on the shared Dialog UI component (src/components/ui/dialog.tsx). This is a reusable pattern that future features may need — any modal that requires forced user action should use this prop. The pattern is clean and well-implemented but not documented in AGENTS.md or the library.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src/components/ui/dialog.tsx:30-37 — hideCloseButton prop added to DialogContentProps. src/components/validation/proxy-failure-modal.tsx:65 — hideCloseButton used.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The worker added many new fields to the ValidationResult interface (isDeliverable, isDisabled, hasFullInbox, canConnectSmtp, acceptsMail, isValidSyntax, isB2c, suggestion, gravatarUrl, haveibeenpwned, proxyId) and removed proxyUsed in the integration commit. This interface expansion was tangential to the failure-modal-ui feature and should have been a separate concern or at minimum documented.

The skill's procedure matched reality well. One minor note: the skill mentions manual verification with agent-browser, but the worker's handoff shows only code-review-level interactive checks (reviewing rendered output) rather than actual browser automation verification.

summary: The failure-modal-ui feature is well-implemented and passes review. The ProxyFailureModal component is clean, properly typed, well-tested (18 tests), and correctly integrated with the Tauri event system. It fulfills all VAL-FLR-002 requirements. Three non-blocking issues identified: one weak test assertion and two handler implementations that were subsequently improved by later features in the same milestone. Two shared state observations noted: the hideCloseButton pattern on Dialog and the tangential ValidationResult interface expansion.
